title: Stephan's Quintet (NIRCam + MIRI Imaging)

geometryEvidence.reference: A picture of the sky: the plane is the picture's own tangent plane, perpendicular to the sight line through the picture's centre, so it faces the Sun. That centre is 24.1 arcsec from the object's position, which is the whole of the recipe's inclination. Not a measured orientation of the object.

registration.method: The file's embedded sky tags, used as they are: 0.09505 arcsec per pixel, north 62.0° right of vertical, the frame's centre at 338.99763°, 33.9604911°. Not measured against Gaia here; the same publishers' tags were within 0.4 arcsec on four cluster pictures and 1.5 arcsec off on one deep field.

displayModel: The picture lies on one flat plane facing the Sun at the object's comoving distance. Nothing in the picture has depth: seen from the side it is a line.
coverage: The published frame inside a circle: the picture fades out between 70% and 98% of half its short side, so its corners are not drawn and no straight edge shows. NGC 7320, the leftmost galaxy, is far in front of the group but stands on the group's plane here. The publisher's 4,000 px Publication JPEG is used; the original is 12,654 px.

acquisition.operation: Download the publisher's JPEG; no crop or resample.
